thread.title: Steep Road Ahead For Tesla To Justify The Premium Valuation - Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)

author: Sapient Investor
title: Steep Road Ahead For Tesla To Justify The Premium Valuation - Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)
text:
Investment Thesis Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) is well-positioned to benefit from a gradual shift in the dynamics of the automobile industry. Tesla has an edge over other companies in the industry due to its head start in manufacturing electric vehicles. Currently, Tesla is perceived to have several competitive advantages due to its hefty investments over the last decade. Although the conventional auto-manufacturers were a bit reluctant to adapt to changing dynamics of the industry, most of them have already realized that it is futile to resist an idea whose time has come. They have already started investing heavily in research and development activities. Almost all the major automobile manufacturers like Audi, BMW, Daimler and Chinese manufacturers have disclosed ambitious plans and targets for the sale of electric vehicles over the next few years. Given the manufacturing expertise of the major players and the ability to allocate huge capital expenditure, we expect competition to intensify over the next decade.
Based on our analysis of Tesla’s economic moat, we expect Tesla’s expertise in the integration of software and hardware to retain its edge over other players. Other perceived advantages like the ability to manufacture batteries more efficiently and having an extensive supercharger network may benefit Tesla, but will not lead to a sustainable competitive advantage, in our view. The role of leadership will be critical for Tesla over the next decade given the rapidly changing dynamics of the industry. The risk associated with the failure to execute Tesla's long-term strategy needs to be considered while analyzing Tesla’s long-term success.
Great Ideas do not necessarily lead to great companies. Great companies do not necessarily lead to great investments. The valuation at which one invests plays a key role in achieving superior returns over the long term. Based on our analysis, we expect Tesla’s current valuation to be running ahead of its fundamentals. Tesla’s current business model may not command a very high valuation multiple, in our view, given the capital requirement of manufacturing companies.
In the base-case scenario, Tesla’s risk-reward ratio does not seem to be favorable to the long-term investors based on the current share price of Tesla. In the base-case scenario, Tesla will continue with its current business model, which is a combination of capital-intensive manufacturing companies and growth-oriented technology companies. We believe that Tesla’s fair valuation multiple should be higher than that of traditional automobile companies but less than that of pure technology companies.
In the most optimistic scenario, Tesla will grow at a much higher pace relative to the industry, driven by new revenue streams associated with self-driving technology. Tesla will be able to maintain much higher operating margins relative to margins of the industry, driven by its superior software capabilities. The business model will become more asset-light either by economies of scale or by outsourcing of the capital-intensive operations, which are not necessary to maintain its edge over peers.
In the most pessimistic scenario, Tesla will lag behind the peers in terms of growth. If the competitors become successful in finding alternative technologies to manufacture batteries more efficiently and collaborate with software providers to get software expertise at a competitive price, Tesla may not be able to maintain margin advantage relative to peers. In this case, the fair valuation multiple may be much lower for Tesla.
Company Introduction Tesla generates revenue primarily by selling electric vehicles. The company handles design, development and manufacturing of electric vehicles. Based on the FY17 reported data, this segment contributes over 80 percent of the revenue for Tesla. Tesla also sells energy storage systems.

Business overview Although the concept of electric vehicles is very old, no one was able to commercialize this concept until recently. Most of the challenges associated with increasing the adoption of electric vehicles seem to be fading away due to heavy investments made by Tesla over the last few years. Currently, Tesla seems to have several competitive advantages relative to its peers. In this report, we tried to analyze the depth and width of those competitive advantages.

Extensive Supercharger Network of Tesla The supercharger network of Tesla offers flexibility and convenience to electric car customers who intend to travel long distances. Currently, Tesla has a dominant position in terms of charging stations in North America. Tesla intends to expand its supercharger network substantially over the next few years across its major markets (North America, Europe and Asia). Although it appears to be an advantage for Tesla over peers, we believe that the depth and width of this competitive advantage are very low. We believe that Tesla has focused on increasing the footprint of electric charger network to make the adoption of electric cars more attractive for customers. At some point of time in future, it may be prudent for Tesla to consider outsourcing or spinning off this segment to focus on its critical core competencies, in our view. There are already quite a few companies (like CHAdeMo and SAE Combo) which focus solely on building electric charger stations. As the adoption of electric vehicles increases we believe the competition in this segment will intensify further in the future. We think this segment to be margin dilutive for Tesla.
Number of publicly available superchargers (Worldwide) in 2017
Source: Statista, IEA, EAFO
The supercharger network will offer certain benefits to the customers of Tesla, but these benefits may not necessarily help Tesla to improve its growth/margin prospects. For example, Tesla’s customers may get a preferential treatment (like lower fee or no fee to charge) compared to the users of other automobile companies, but this may not play a critical role in the customer’s buying decision as we expect the cost of recharging the electric vehicle to be significantly lower than the fuel prices. So, customers may be indifferent to this aspect while making a choice of their automobile. Moreover, customers have a provision to charge their vehicles at their homes overnight. This implies that the supercharger network's usage is very limited. In addition, Tesla’s supercharger network is open to cater to electric vehicles manufactured by other companies. So, this will not be a unique benefit available only for Tesla customers. Therefore, we believe that Tesla may not be able to charge a premium price for their cars relative to other manufacturers based on this factor.

Mammoth Giga-factories to drive the prices of electric vehicles lower The main strategic motive underlying Tesla’s focus on building mammoth giga-factories to produce batteries for electric vehicles is to make the electric cars more affordable. Affordability is one of the key factors in driving the proliferation of electric cars, in our view. Currently, the cost of a battery forms a significant portion of the overall cost of manufacturing an electric vehicle. The battery costs have fallen substantially over the last decade, but there is still a long way to go before the batteries of electric cars become affordable enough to make the electric vehicles more popular among the masses. Tesla intends to bring down the cost of producing the batteries substantially by opting to set up its latest giga-factory in China. Given the cost benefits related to manufacturing in China, we are confident over this strategy of Tesla. We have already seen the role played by Chinese smartphone manufacturers in promoting the proliferation of smartphone penetration by making affordable smartphones.
Worldwide Market share of Li-Ion Battery Manufacturers (Q1 2018)
Source: www.electrive.com , Statista
From a strategy point of view, we think Tesla is doing the right thing at this stage. The creation of these giga-factories will accelerate the evolution of the automobile industry. Tesla has higher stakes than anyone in the evolution of conventional automobile industry supported by internal combustible engines into an industry supported by electric vehicles. Tesla seems to be much ahead of its peers by leapfrogging into manufacturing the batteries for electric vehicles. Based on the reported production capacity numbers, Tesla would become the largest manufacturer of batteries for electric vehicles over the next few years.
But, this may not necessarily lead to a sustainable competitive advantage for Tesla. Technology advantage is the most difficult form of competitive advantage to sustain. In an optimistic scenario, Tesla would continue to produce electric vehicles at a lower price and achieve better margins relative to the peers. But this margin advantage would come at the expense of managing a highly risky and capital-intensive task of operating several large-scale manufacturing plants.
Battery Electric Vehicle cost breakdown by type (%) as of 2018
Source: JPMC, BCG, Statista
Invention of alternative technologies in battery production may pose a serious threat to profitability of these giga-factories. Tesla is relying on Lithium-Ion batteries and currently, major automobile players are investing in research to develop batteries which rely on alternative technologies like Lithium-Sulfur, Zinc-Air, Aluminium-ion, Smart membranes and Graphene-based supercapacitors, etc. to develop batteries which are more efficient in terms of cost, lifespan and the ability to charge faster. Irrespective of the success of their efforts, we believe the battery prices will go down gradually over next few years driven by the improvements in current technology.
Based on a study done by Bloomberg New Energy Finance, battery cost will reduce to around 16% of the cost of manufacturing an electric vehicle compared to the current level of 37%. We believe that this phenomenon will benefit the overall Industry by improving the affordability of customers and thereby increasing the penetration of electric vehicles.
Currently, Tesla seems to be ahead of other players in the industry in terms of battery range, time taken to charge faster and the costs associated with manufacturing batteries. However, we believe that rival companies to close this gap with Tesla eventually by relying on alternate technologies or by partnering with battery manufacturers like Panasonic ( OTCPK:PCRFY ) (Tesla’s partner) to emulate Tesla’s technology. The quality of battery may not be a significant differentiating factor among various automobile manufacturers over the long term, in our view. Therefore, we believe that although these giga-factories may be beneficial to the overall automobile industry evolution, this may not lead to a sustainable economic moat for Tesla over the long term.

Source: Statista, Autotrader.com , data as of April 2017
Software Integration with the Hardware As the automobile industry is set to undergo a material transformation over the next few years driven by entry of electric vehicles, automobile companies with superior software skills will be at an advantage compared to conventional automobile companies which resist to change. Currently, Tesla seems to be much ahead of other conventional automobile companies in terms of software and hardware integration. Tesla’s software has a digital control over its brakes, steering and motor. The performance of hardware can be improved in a faster (over the air) way by using the data collected from its inbuilt integrated autopilot hardware subsystems.
As Tesla builds a customized software suitable for its vehicles, the integration of software and hardware will be much smoother and efficient. This feature may not appear to be ground-breaking at this stage, but would play a critical role in the future. Unlike the conventional cars which have only a limited usage, the next generation electric cars will have much more utility with the advent of autonomous driving technology. At this stage it is being predicted that cars can be used as a software application to generate revenue when not in use. For example, self-driving cars can be used as ride-sharing vehicles or as food-delivery vehicles. It may be hard to anticipate many other modes of utility of vehicles post the advent of self-driving technology. Therefore, we believe that the ability of an automobile manufacturer to handle software and hardware integration would be a key factor in making a decision to buy a car.
The automobile operators with in-house software capabilities will be at an advantage, in our view. However, the conventional automobile players which lack the software expertise may have to partner with other software providers like Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) or Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ). This may not result in a perfect software and hardware integration but the third-party software providers like Google may offer many more attractive features at a lower price. It will be hard to say who will dominate the market at this stage, but it appears that Tesla has a clear advantage compared to other players at this stage. Over the long term, Tesla should focus more on this aspect of superior software capability to differentiate itself from other players rather than focusing on other aspects like expanding service centers and dealership centers, charging station network or battery producing units, etc.
Leadership/Vision to play a critical role over next decade Elon Musk has been successful so far in driving Tesla towards a clear goal of making it the leader in an Industry, which is awaiting a massive disruption. He was among the first few who could envision the entire eco-system that is necessary to succeed in an automobile industry dominated by Technology. But, we believe that the role of his leadership will be even more critical over the next few years due to the intensifying competition and threat of alternative technologies.
The leaders who transform good companies into great have a common quality. It is a paradoxical blend of humility and professional will. They channel their ego needs away from themselves and into the larger goal of building a great company. It’s not that they have no ego or self-interest. Indeed, they are incredibly ambitious-but their ambition is first and foremost for the institution, not themselves (Source: Good to Great by Jim Collins).
Elon Musk’s capability to steer Tesla in the right direction is beyond doubt for anyone following Tesla for last few years. But it worries us when he focuses his efforts on short-term share price boosting tactics like making ambitious announcements/targets to boost shareholder sentiment. Tesla missed on several sales targets mentioned by Musk so far. He may lose credibility over long term if this pattern continues. He should realize that underpromising and overdelivering on the results will build credibility, which commands a sustainable valuation premium over the long term. Tesla needs to go a long way to justify the capital injected into the company so far. If Elon Musk wants to boost the valuation, he should focus more on the aspects related to the business which improve the return on invested capital for Tesla.
Right now, Tesla is handling far too many responsibilities than it can handle, in our view. For example, Tesla intends to handle all the aspects ranging from designing, manufacturing, marketing, selling, servicing, building own charger network and manufacturing batteries for electric vehicles. All these activities may not be equally important to maintain a dominant position in the industry. Some of the activities may be either too capital-intensive or margin-dilutive and may be interfering with Tesla’s ability to focus on its real core competencies. Therefore, we believe that there is a huge risk associated with the execution of strategy for Tesla.
It’s undeniable that there are some benefits associated with handling all the activities in-house. For example, Tesla can provide superior customer service by handling its own service centers and offer discounts to its customers at the charging stations. But we don’t believe that these things make Tesla outstanding compared to peers. As the electric vehicle industry is set to enter the growth stage soon, competition may get tougher. It may be tougher to compete with automobile companies with manufacturing expertise (with huge scale advantage) who may collaborate with software providers like Google having expertise in software capabilities. We believe that Tesla would be justifying its premium valuation by focusing on its software-hardware integration. However, it may not be an easy job. The top management of Tesla should be able to envision the future of the industry realistically and steer Tesla in the right direction, because it is going to be the toughest decade ahead for Tesla.
Having great Ideas doesn’t necessarily result in great companies. Finding great companies doesn’t necessarily result in great Investments. The valuation at which one invests plays a key role in determining the potential return. We have analyzed Tesla’s valuation considering various scenarios.

Valuation We use a relative valuation multiple based on EV/EBITDA to determine the value of Tesla. The companies in the automobile industry like Fiat Chrysler (NYSE: FCAU ), Ford Motor (NYSE: F ) and General Motors (NYSE: GM ) are not comparable to Tesla based on the underlying fundamentals. These companies have limited growth prospects due to saturation of sales in most of the markets. Moreover, their capital intensity is very high due to the nature of the manufacturing industry. Therefore, they command very low valuation multiples.

Based on the above data, we observe that Capex/EBITDA plays a prominent role in determining the fair valuation multiple (EV/EBITDA). As we believe Tesla’s capital intensity to be higher than all the technology companies mentioned above, we prefer to use a fair valuation multiple lower than any of them. Although we believe that growth prospects of Tesla may be better than the growth prospects of Facebook, we think Tesla will be slightly more capital intensive. We prefer to remain cautious and use a 1 year forward EV/EBITDA multiple of 8.1 (based on 15% discount to the valuation multiple of Facebook), in our base case scenario.
We estimate the revenue growth to be around 26% (CAGR) over 2018-25 based on projected increase in sale of electric vehicles and decline in the average price of the vehicles. In our base case scenario, we assume the revenue growth for Tesla to be 26% (CAGR) over 2018-25e in line with the industry sales growth. We estimate the 2018e revenue by assuming the Q4 2018 revenue to be equal to that of Q3 2018e reported revenue.

Risks to our analysis Upside risks: Revenue growth may be higher than expected, driven by the new streams of revenue driven by self-driving technology. Operating margins can be higher if the new sources of revenue have higher margins. Capital intensity may be much lower than we expect due to technological advancements.
Downside risks: Competition may get intense and other players may engage in a price war to tackle Tesla’s technology advantage. Competitors may close the gap with Tesla in terms of technological expertise. High valuation multiple may not be sustainable if there is a risk associated with the execution of the long-term strategy.
Advice to Investors Investors should have a very long-term horizon to invest in a company like Tesla. They should not worry about each and every news (tweet) related to Tesla (Elon Musk). They should not get overly bullish by Tesla’s ambitious announcements related to sales targets. At the same time, they should not worry if Tesla misses some of its near-term targets. It is important to have an idea of the larger picture. Even if you believe that Tesla’s business model is not viable and the stock price is overvalued, it may not be prudent to short Tesla. Shorting a stock is usually a very risky strategy as the market can remain irrational for longer than you can stay solvent.
It is very hard to anticipate the growth prospects and looming risks ahead of time for an industry, which is set to undergo radical changes. For example, Tesla can surprise the entire market by generating revenues from a new stream in the future with the advent of self-driving cars. At the same time, some of the technologies of Tesla may become obsolete if the rival companies become successful in their research and development efforts. Therefore, it is always better to rely on conservative estimates to focus on the preservation of capital. Based on our conservative estimates, the current risk-reward ratio is more skewed towards risk for long-term investors.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
